summary: Nicolae Ceaușescu rose from a teenage communist agitator to dictator of Romania (1965-1989), courting the West while ruining the economy, banning abortion, filling orphanages, expanding the Securitate and razing villages until he was overthrown and shot in 1989.

evidence.note: born January 1918 to a poor peasant family in Scornicești
Gheorghiu-Dej dies in March 1965 and Ceaușescu becomes party leader
he and Elena are tried and shot on Christmas Day 1989
contraception and abortion banned to raise population; thousands of women die
1968 speech condemning the Soviet invasion of Czechoslovakia wins Western favour
1971 tour of China and North Korea inspires his personality cult
Jewish emigrants ransomed to Israel for cash on a sliding scale
Securitate phone-tapping and informant network expands massively
preventable deaths and neglect of children in state institutions
HIV spreads among orphans, mostly Roma, through blood transfusions
Tőkés eviction sparks Timișoara protests that grow into revolution

notes: Transcript gives the birth date as 23 January 1918; sources say 26 January. Long opening background (Vlad III, 1907 revolt, WWI, Iron Guard, Antonescu) is context before the story and does not extend covered_span; fascism-far-right left out for that reason. Post-1989 orphan aftermath and prosecutions are a short coda, so reaches_present is false.
